question.title: Bin Sweeper
question.content:
A sorting line has several bins of parcels. A sweeper visits the bins in rounds: in each round it goes through the bins in order and takes the first parcel left in each bin that still has one. Implement the BinSweeper class:

  • BinSweeper(List<List<Integer>> bins) Sets the sweeper up over bins.
  • boolean hasNext() Returns true if any parcel is left.
  • int next() Returns the next parcel the sweeper takes.

 

Example 1:

Input
["BinSweeper", "hasNext", "next", "next", "next", "hasNext"]
[[[[8,2],[],[6]]], [], [], [], [], []]
Output
[null, true, 8, 6, 2, false]

Explanation
BinSweeper binSweeper = new BinSweeper([[8,2],[],[6]]);
binSweeper.hasNext(); // return true
binSweeper.next();    // return 8, the first round starts
binSweeper.next();    // return 6, the middle bin is empty
binSweeper.next();    // return 2, the second round
binSweeper.hasNext(); // return false

Example 2:

Input
["BinSweeper", "next", "next", "hasNext", "next", "next", "hasNext"]
[[[[11],[14,16,19]]], [], [], [], [], [], []]
Output
[null, 11, 14, true, 16, 19, false]

Example 3:

Input
["BinSweeper", "hasNext"]
[[[[],[]]], []]
Output
[null, false]

 

Constraints:

  • 1 <= bins.length <= 100
  • 0 <= bins[i].size() <= 100
  • 0 <= bins[i][j] <= 1000
  • next is only called when a parcel is left.
  • At most 104 calls will be made to hasNext and next.
